questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: When you inspect brakes, look for these problems: cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign that a person is drowsy?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous. Signs of drowsiness include blinking often, your eyes closing or going out of focus by themselves, yawning often, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: Loading weight so the center of gravity is high:

options.text: Makes the vehicle more likely to roll over.
Makes items fall down more easily.
Makes it harder to unload the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the vehicle more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: When cargo is loaded with a high center of gravity, the vehicle is more likely to tip over. Always load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums during your walk-around inspection before you drive. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: Texting while driving is dangerous because:

options.text: It distracts you both mentally and physically.
Texts may be more interesting than driving.
It is slower than making a phone call.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts you both mentally and physically.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is a serious distraction because it takes your mind and your hands away from driving.

questions.question: Driving a refrigerated truck with hanging meat:

options.text: Is good practice for new drivers.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable cargo. It has a high center of gravity and swings as you drive, making it harder to control the vehicle. You need driving skill to handle this load safely.

questions.question: ABS helps you to:
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up during hard braking. Drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: Radial and bias-ply tires:

options.text: Can be used together on all axles.
Can be used together only on the rear axle.

questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure you do not use radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: You cannot see behind the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front.
Trailers cannot be driven in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only back up if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: Always assume a train is coming when you approach a railroad crossing. Do not rely on signals or your ears to tell you if a train is present. Always slow down at a crossing. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Stop cargo from moving during transport.
Stop cargo from being loaded too high.
Stop cargo from being unloaded too quickly.
Stop cargo from being unloaded easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from sliding during transport.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers notice road hazards more slowly than focused drivers. Sometimes they do not notice hazards at all.

questions.question: Passive railroad crossings:

options.text: Have gates that lower when trains are near.
Should never be crossed by a CMV.

questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: Good drivers look ____ seconds ahead of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of their vehicle. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Which one is not a type of distraction?
questions.explanation: Distractions are physical (like reaching for an object), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like using a hand-held phone).

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum happens when brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Do not use the parking brake when parking if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.
There is water on the ground.

questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if brakes are very hot from going down a steep hill or if they are wet in freezing weather. Hot brakes can be damaged. Wet brakes in freezing weather can ice up and lock the vehicle.

questions.question: Brake fade is caused by:
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they get too hot. This heat causes brake fade, which makes brakes less effective.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Can make a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make a vehicle more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: If a train is approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across the tracks. It is hard to judge a train's speed. Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.question: What is a drawback of retarders?

options.text: They may not be allowed in all places.
They can help slow a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be allowed in all places.
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, these devices can be loud and are not allowed everywhere.

questions.question: If stopped on the road or shoulder, within 10 minutes you must:

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and wave traffic to pass.

questions.explanation: If stopped on the side of the road, you must place emergency warning devices, such as reflective triangles, within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive forward past the parking space. Then back into it, bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the back of the space. Your vehicle should fit completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly to:

options.text: Avoid losing control of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on slippery surfaces. Using too much power can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, reduce your speed for safety.

questions.question: When traveling down a slope, a vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.explanation: Gravity causes a vehicle's speed to increase going downhill. Choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight before going down a slope.

questions.question: When a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) starts:

options.text: The ABS light turns on, then quickly turns off.
The steering wheel won't move until air tanks are full.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS light turns on, then quickly turns off.
questions.explanation: After starting an ABS vehicle, the indicator light should come on and then turn off. If the light stays on, the ABS has a problem.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help you see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles use curved convex mirrors. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when using a cell phone or doing something physical.
Can happen from mental activities like daydreaming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen from mental activities like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Mental distractions are as dangerous as physical ones. You can look at a hazard but fail to see it if your mind is on something else.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Use the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it damages tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parked. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: When trying to avoid a hazard:

options.text: Swerving may work better than stopping.
You can change lanes without looking.
You should drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may work better than stopping.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. You can usually turn away from a hazard faster than you can stop completely. However, swerving has risks too, like rolling over in a heavy vehicle or one pulling trailers.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, the S-cam:

options.text: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Pushes the brake lining against the wheel.
Lets air out of the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, the S-cam pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: A five-foot-long item on a flatbed trailer must be secured with at least:
questions.explanation: Cargo should have one tie-down for every 10 feet of length. However, always use at least two tie-downs, no matter how small the cargo is.

questions.question: While driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used because they are distracting.
Not be used unless there is traffic.

questions.explanation: You need to know what is around you at all times. Check your mirrors often to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: Which of these is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your tires carefully before driving. Tire sizes must match. Do not use tires that are cut, cracked, or damaged in any way.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when you do something physical while driving.
Can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for something), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you leave, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.

questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is very important at night.

questions.question: Hazardous material placards must be at least:
questions.explanation: Hazardous material placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a CMV, the operator should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Not worry about speed, just focus on the road.
Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing down gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect how slowly your CMV must go to make a tight turn safely. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them ahead of time.

questions.question: Why should you be careful around rental trucks?

options.text: Rental vehicles usually do not have insurance.
Drivers are usually worried about their cargo.
Drivers may not be used to the limited views to the sides and rear.
They do not respond to braking as well as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may not be used to the limited views to the sides and rear.
questions.explanation: You should be careful around rental trucks. The drivers may not be used to operating vehicles with limited views to the sides and rear. Drivers who cannot see other vehicles are a hazard on the road.

questions.question: When checking power steering hoses before a trip, look for:

options.text: Extra hose pieces available for repairs.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle before a trip, check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look closely at the hoses for any leaks.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle than yours:

options.text: Usually stops faster than your vehicle.
Usually takes longer to stop than your vehicle.
Takes about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually stops faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far to stay behind other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before pressing down hard.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you slow or stop.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS. When ABS works properly, it automatically engages when braking in situations that may cause the wheels to lock.

questions.question: When making a left turn with two turn lanes, start in the right lane because:

options.text: It is easier to see other turning vehicles on your left than on your right.
Your vehicle will turn more quickly.
Other vehicles will get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is easier to see other turning vehicles on your left than on your right.
questions.explanation: When turning left with multiple turn lanes available, use the right turn lane. Large vehicles need to swing right to turn left. It is safer to have other turning traffic on your left rather than your right. This gives you a better view of other turning vehicles and reduces collision risk.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a potentially drunk driver?

options.text: They stay in their traffic lane.
They drive at a consistent speed.

questions.explanation: Warning signs of an impaired driver include trouble staying in their lane, trouble keeping a steady speed, or stopping for no clear reason.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment:

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine, make sure the parking brake is on and the wheels are chocked. Check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: If someone pulls in front of you and you cannot stop, you should:

options.text: Hit the other vehicle since it is their fault.
Swerve to avoid the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerve to avoid the other car.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle pulls in front of you, brake if you have room to stop. If you do not have room to stop, swerving is a safer option.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under a bridge, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Not make gestures to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make gestures to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan trips with extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane. Do not make gestures at other drivers.
